messages:
leo: Heads-up — seeing an increase in streaming token jitter and some grpc deadline_exceeded from eu-west dedicated pool (nvlink). Spike started ~08:04 UTC, p95 token latency ~2x. Anyone else?
anya: yup saw alerts on the cost/latency dashboard. spike aligns with a cluster rebalancer job that started at 08:02.
sam: I ran a quick tail on the grpc logs: lots of \"deadline_exceeded\" and a few \"context canceled\" correlated with long token streams.
mike: can we repro with iperf between two affected pods/nodes? last time reordering was due to MTU mismatch on overlay.
leo: ran iperf3 from pod A -> pod B (same rack, different host):
```
# iperf3 -c podB -t 10 -J
{"end": {"sum": {"seconds": 10, "retransmits": 0, "sender_bytes": 12345678}}}
```
iperf shows decent throughput, but packet-level capture shows out-of-order and high inter-packet jitter.
anya: pasted tcpdump snippet from the sidecar capture: 
```
15:08:06.123456 IP 10.0.3.5.54012 > 10.0.2.9.9000: Flags [.], seq 12345:12445, ack 54321, win 64240, length 100
15:08:06.123457 IP 10.0.3.5.54012 > 10.0.2.9.9000: Flags [.], seq 12245:12345, ack 54321, win 64240, length 100  # out-of-order
```
sam: that's classic reordering. ethtool stats on the host show increasing rx_missed and rx_no_buffer on ena0. snippet: `ethtool -S ena0 | grep rx` -> "rx_missed 128"
mike: could be GSO/GRO or hardware offload interaction with VXLAN/ENI. Also check MTU across the entire path.
leo: checked `ip link` on the two hosts — one has MTU 9000, the other 1450 (we've got a broken host migration).
anya: ohhh that's likely it. VXLAN + mismatched MTU => fragmentation and reassembly causing reordering/jitter for streams.
sre-oncall: temporarily marking affected nodes as draining to stop new streams. I've added a placement rule to avoid eu-west-b pool while we investigate.
leo: quick mitigation: disabling GRO/GSO on the affected host reduced out-of-order events in next 5m window. command used: `sudo ethtool -K ens4 gro off gso off`
mike: long-term fix is to enforce MTU uniformity and prevent mixed host images in the same pool. Also need a check in node-join to validate MTU vs cluster setting.
sam: for streaming infra we should also harden the rpc client to tolerate modest reordering/jitter (replay buffer, slightly higher per-stream deadline, backpressure). raising deadline from 2s -> 3s reduced customer-visible errors.
leo: cost/ops note: routing traffic away from eu-west for a few hours increases cross-region egress; ops estimate ~ $300 extra if we keep it for 6h.
anya: action items: 1) enforce MTU check on node join (mike), 2) roll nodes to unify MTU (infra), 3) add preflight that rejects mixes (leo), 4) add streaming backpressure + deadline tuning (sam).
devops-bot: incident created: INCIDENT-2026-042, severity P2, assigned to eng-runtime + eng-infra.
sre-oncall: scheduling maintenance window tonight 02:00 UTC to roll affected eu-west nodes and update the node-join script. I'll coordinate with infra.
leo: notes: avoid immediate mass restart — do staggered drains to keep capacity. Also add temporary fallback: route long-running streams to non-eu hosts where possible (canary traffic already shows improved p95).
mike: follow-up: we'll add a CI check for MTU and a calico policy to prevent VNIs with mismatched MTU from being attached.
anya: I'll update the postmortem template with a networking checklist (MTU, GSO/GRO, offload stats, ena counters).
sam: small snippet to detect reordering in tcpdump: `tcpdump -tt -n -r /tmp/capture.pcap | awk '/out-of-order/ {print}'` (not perfect but helped).
leo: thanks all — keeping the thread for runbook updates. If anyone sees reordering after the roll tonight ping here. :thumbsup:
